caption: Florida student arrested after Netanyahu “bomb joke” in WhatsApp group.

A student at Florida International University in Miami was arrested after posting messages in a large WhatsApp group that authorities interpreted as a bomb threat involving Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

The 23-year-old student, Gabriela Saldana, allegedly wrote in a chat with about 215 students discussing a campus event: “Netanyahu, if you can hear me, drop some bonbons for us…” at the university's Ocean Bank Convocation Center. Investigators said “bonbons” was interpreted as a reference to bombs.
Police said she later sent another message claiming “there is going to be a bomb” at the venue, which triggered reports from other students and prompted a campus police investigation.

Saldana was arrested near the campus and charged with making written threats to kill or cause bodily harm, a second-degree felony in Florida that can carry up to 15 years in prison. Bail was set at $5,000.
She later told the group chat the message was “a dumb joke that should not have been made,” but a judge said the messages could still be considered a credible threat regardless of intent.
